class.name: NetwSessionHandle
class.brief_description: The session plane of one session, gathered onto one object.
class.description: A client over the [code]session_*[/code], [code]player_*[/code], [code]peer_*[/code] and [code]stats_*[/code] families on [NetwMultiplayer], reached as [method Netw.session] from any [Node]. Every member forwards to a flat verb, and the flat verb is the stable spelling: this repository's own suites, examples and browser call [NetwMultiplayer] directly, and a game reaches for this when it would rather hold the plane as one object. [codeblock] var s := Netw.session(self) s.entered.connect(on_entered) s.disconnected.connect(on_over) s.ended.connect(on_over) for player: NetwPlayer in s.players: scoreboard.add(player) [/codeblock] [b]What this object buys over the flat surface is its signals.[/b] [Netw] is static and a static class publishes none, so a game that wants to hear a session's edges has to name the session to hear them. This object is where they are named once: [signal entered], [signal ended], [signal disconnected], [signal disconnecting], [signal player_joined], [signal local_joined], [signal player_left], [signal join_failed], [signal scene_live], [signal scene_changed] and [signal presentation_changed], all relayed from the session that created it. One handle exists per session for the life of that session, so a game may hold it across an await. [signal disconnected] is the one member that relays a signal this framework does not own. [signal MultiplayerAPI.server_disconnected] is Godot's and stays reachable on [code]multiplayer[/code]; it is re-emitted here so one object returns every cause a session has to end, which is what a game pairing it with [signal ended] under one handler actually wants. Bringing a session UP is not on this object. A session comes online the ordinary Godot way, by assigning a [MultiplayerPeer] to [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer], the connect plane is [NetwConnectHandle] reached as [method Netw.connection], and joining is [method Netw.prepare_join], which routes prepare against submit off session state. This object is what a session already up admits, reports, and tears down.

method.name: bucket_of
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_bucket]: the per-peer bucket of [param type] that [param peer] carries, [code]null[/code] when it carries none.

method.name: kick
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.player_kick]: ends [param player]'s membership and turns their peer away carrying [param reason], which holds the law and the errors. This ends a membership rather than closing a connection, and [method leave] is how a peer ends its own. The local server's player is refused here for that reason. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: leave
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.session_leave]: leaves the session this handle was created by, returning the promise that resolves once the peer is down.

method.name: player_of
method.description: The [NetwPlayer] this session holds for [param peer], [code]null[/code] when it holds none. Forwards to [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_player], which is the same result under the flat spelling.

method.name: request_scene
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_request]: asks server authority for the scene at [param path] over [param scope], one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.SceneChange], returning the promise that resolves when the scene is live or rejects when authority declines. A scene already live is reached by [method Netw.scene] and read through its own [NetwSceneHandle]; this verb is the asking. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: set_server_info
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.session_set_server_info]: replaces what this session advertises about itself, at runtime, so a name a player typed reaches the listing rather than the snapshot the session started from. [b]Server Only.[/b]

members.member: A [NetwSessionConfig] SNAPSHOT of what this session was configured with. Each read creates a new one and writing to it changes nothing, which is [method NetwMultiplayer.session_get_config]'s own contract: the live edits are [method Netw.configure_session] before the session comes up and [method set_server_info] after.
Whether this peer is a client of a session hosted elsewhere, so a listen-server host reads [code]false[/code] here. [member NetwMultiplayer.is_local_client].
Whether this session has a peer assigned and connected. [member NetwMultiplayer.is_online].
The [NetwPlayer] this session holds for this peer, [code]null[/code] before the local join is accepted. [signal local_joined] is the edge that fills it.

The scene this peer draws, [code]null[/code] while it draws none. A game writes nothing to reach it. [signal presentation_changed] is its edge and [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_presented] is the flat reading. It follows where this peer is, so it is a local reading and no other peer sees anything of it. [method NetwSceneHandle.watch] is the separate verb that decides what a player actually receives. [codeblock lang=text] one scene holds a body of this peer that scene no body, one scene this peer watches that scene bodies in two, or two watched nothing, with a warning neither nothing [/codeblock] Two worlds at once draw nothing rather than one of them, because a peer standing in two places is a question only the game can answer and a framework answering it draws the wrong world in silence. On a listen server this is what [HostSceneView] draws, because only a host runs scenes in worlds of their own. Several bodies in the presented scene each hear [signal NetwEntity.view_activated], and the camera is adopted automatically only where exactly one of them is local.

Every [NetwPlayer] that has joined, including rows whose peer has since gone, which is what [member NetwMultiplayer.players] returns and is the roster a scoreboard wants. The rows still CONNECTED are [member NetwMultiplayer.connected_players].
What this peer is in the session, one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.Role]. [member NetwMultiplayer.role].
The [Node] this session's replicated branch hangs under, [code]null[/code] when the session is not mounted. [member NetwMultiplayer.root].

Every live scene, as the [NetwSceneHandle] each one is read through. The session keys its rows by an internal handle, and that handle never crosses onto this view: a caller naming one scene reaches for [method Netw.scene] instead.
[method NetwMultiplayer.stats_snapshot]: every counter this session keeps, keyed by the [enum NetwMultiplayer.Stat] constant that names it.

signal.name: disconnected
signal.description: Relayed from [signal MultiplayerAPI.server_disconnected]: the server this peer was connected to is gone, without having said so first. Godot's own signal, re-emitted here so one object returns every cause a session has to end. [signal ended] is the same event when this peer's own session tore down, and [signal disconnecting] is the host announcing it in advance.

signal.name: disconnecting
signal.description: The server has announced that it is going down, carrying [param reason]. [signal disconnected] is what arrives when it does not announce.

signal.name: ended
signal.description: This session has torn down. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_ended].

signal.name: entered
signal.description: This peer's join was accepted and the session is live for it. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_entered].

signal.name: join_failed
signal.description: This peer's own join was turned down, carrying the [param code] and the [param reason] the server gave. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_join_failed]. No membership was created, so [member local_player] is still [code]null[/code] and [signal local_joined] never fires for that attempt. [method Netw.prepare_join]'s promise reports only that the request went out, so this is where a refusal arrives.

signal.name: local_joined
signal.description: The [NetwPlayer] the session holds for THIS peer has joined, which is also when [member local_player] starts returning. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.player_local_joined].

signal.name: presentation_changed
signal.description: The scene this peer draws has changed, carrying the handle left and the one taken, either of which may be [code]null[/code]. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.scene_presentation_changed]. [member presented_scene] is what changed and how it is derived. Spent on a change and never on a repeat. It is the edge a move across worlds lands on, because the body that arrives is a new object on the peer that owns it and this announces the arrival rather than the object.

signal.name: player_joined
signal.description: A [NetwPlayer] has joined, this peer's own row included. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.player_joined].

signal.name: player_left
signal.description: A [NetwPlayer]'s membership has ended, whether their peer disconnected or [method kick] ended it. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.player_left], which carries the ordering. [member NetwPlayer.is_active] already reads [code]false[/code] here, so this is the last edge at which a game can read the handle it filed that player under and erase its own row for them.

signal.name: scene_changed
signal.description: A [method Netw.change_scene_to_file] has landed. [param scene] is the destination and [param arrived] holds the players it brought there. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.scene_changed]. A change carries no body, so this is where the server gives the arrivals one. A player already watching the destination is not in [param arrived], so a repeated change announces nobody and the spawn happens once. [codeblock] func _on_scene_changed( scene: NetwSceneHandle, arrived: Array[NetwPlayer]) -> void: for who in arrived: scene.root.add_child( Netw.spawn_player(who, make_player)) [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

signal.name: scene_live
signal.description: A scene is live and reachable, carrying the [NetwSceneHandle] it is read through. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.scene_live]. This is where a game puts what a scene needs, and the handle it is handed is the one to keep. Watching a player, observing an edge, and reading the scene's entities are all members on it. It fires once the scene root is ready, so the whole scene is mounted and a handler may reach into it. Their [member Node.multiplayer] answers and their [code]@onready[/code] fields are set. [codeblock] func _on_scene_live(arena: NetwSceneHandle) -> void: arena.root.get_node(^"Spawns").arrange() [/codeblock]
